findings.title: task 3.1: the jwks keys check inspects only the first key, not 'at least one' RS256 key
findings.detail: Task 3.1 check 2 requires that `keys` holds at least one key with `alg` RS256 and a non-empty kid, n and e. checkJwks asserts these on `keys[0]` only. Real Keycloak JWKS often lists an RSA-OAEP encryption key alongside the signing key, so the contract can fail against Keycloak even though a valid RS256 key is present. [rejected by the delegate (claude-fable-5-1 via claude-code) (The finding holds. Task 3.1 check 2 says the JWKS must hold at least one key with alg RS256 and non-empty kid, n and e, and the spec says the contract suite must pass on real Keycloak as well as on the fake. checkJwks in contract.ts takes keys[0] and asserts alg RS256 and the fields on that single key, so a JWKS whose first entry is a non-RS256 key (as Keycloak publishes an RSA-OAEP encryption key beside the signing key) fails the check although a valid RS256 key is present. The check must search the array for an RS256 key instead of inspecting the first entry. WHEN the jwks keys check fetches a JWKS whose keys array holds a valid RS256 key with non-empty kid, n and e at any position, with other keys of another alg before it THEN the check resolves, and it still rejects with an AssertionError when no key of the array has alg RS256 with non-empty kid, n and e.)]
findings.suggested_fix: Find a key with `alg === "RS256"` in `keys` and assert kid, n and e on that key.

findings.title: Successful and error redirects are re-serialised by URL, so the Location can differ from the registered string
findings.detail: redirectReply builds the Location with `new URL(redirectUri)` and `searchParams.set`. A redirect registered as `http://127.0.0.1:9` therefore gets `/` added, and an existing query is re-encoded. The criteria require exact string matching on input but do not pin the output form.
findings.suggested_fix: WHEN a client registered with the redirect `http://127.0.0.1:9` signs in successfully THEN the `Location` is `http://127.0.0.1:9/?code=<code>&state=<state>`, with the path `/` added by URL serialisation.

findings.title: Sign-in POST reads username and password from the query before the form body
findings.detail: param() returns the query value when one exists and falls back to the form only otherwise. A POST with `username` or `password` in the query therefore ignores the posted form value.
findings.suggested_fix: WHEN a sign-in POST carries `username` both in the query and in the form body THEN the query value is used and the form value is ignored.

findings.title: verifyRs256 also requires the header kid to equal the JWK kid
findings.detail: Design decision 5 says verifyRs256 is true for alg RS256 plus a matching signature. The implementation also returns false when the header kid differs from the JWK's kid, so a token signed by the right key under another kid fails. This affects how 'the current key's signature checks' can be shown for the unknown_kid flaw.
findings.suggested_fix: WHEN `verifyRs256` gets a token signed by the JWK's private key whose header `kid` differs from the JWK's `kid` THEN it returns false.

findings.title: Oversized bodies are read to the end before the 413
findings.detail: readBody keeps consuming data after the limit is passed, discarding it, and answers only at `end`. A huge upload is fully received before the 413 is sent and the socket destroyed.
findings.suggested_fix: WHEN a request body exceeds 65536 bytes THEN the server reads and discards the whole body before it answers 413 `{"error":"invalid_request"}` and destroys the socket.

findings.title: Leftover scaffold stub comments and a misleading close error code
findings.detail: jwt.ts and keys.ts still begin with 'Signature stub (milestone scaffold...)' although they are now implemented. close() rejects with FAKE_OIDC_START_FAILED when the server fails to close.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the stub comments and use a fitting error for a failed close.

findings.title: Userinfo accepts an ID token as the bearer
findings.detail: liveAccessToken in session.ts checks the signature, iss, exp and sid, but never typ. A valid ID token (typ "ID") sent as a bearer gets a 200 profile, although the requirement says "live access token". No scenario pins this.
findings.suggested_fix: WHEN userinfo is called with a valid, unexpired ID token of a live session as the bearer THEN it answers 200 with the profile claims.

findings.title: mintJwt treats an unknown kind as an ID token
findings.detail: mintJwt picks access claims only when kind === "access". Any other value, for example "refresh" cast in, silently gives an ID token, where unknown user, client and flaw all throw.
findings.suggested_fix: WHEN mintToken gets a kind other than "id" or "access" THEN it returns a valid ID token without throwing.

findings.title: wrong_nonce without a nonce yields "-mismatch"
findings.detail: applyClaimFlaw writes `${nonce ?? ""}-mismatch`, so wrong_nonce with no nonce option gives nonce "-mismatch". No scenario covers it.
findings.suggested_fix: WHEN mintToken gets flaw wrong_nonce and no nonce THEN the token's nonce claim is "-mismatch".

human.reason: The finding holds. findings.title: task 3.1: the jwks keys check inspects only the first key, not 'at least one' RS256 key
findings.detail: Task 3.1 check 2 requires that `keys` holds at least one key with `alg` RS256 and a non-empty kid, n and e. checkJwks asserts these on `keys[0]` only. Real Keycloak JWKS often lists an RSA-OAEP encryption key alongside the signing key, so the contract can fail against Keycloak even though a valid RS256 key is present.
findings.suggested_fix: Find a key with `alg === "RS256"` in `keys` and assert kid, n and e on that key.

findings.title: Successful and error redirects are re-serialised by URL, so the Location can differ from the registered string
findings.detail: redirectReply builds the Location with `new URL(redirectUri)` and `searchParams.set`. A redirect registered as `http://127.0.0.1:9` therefore gets `/` added, and an existing query is re-encoded. The criteria require exact string matching on input but do not pin the output form.
findings.suggested_fix: WHEN a client registered with the redirect `http://127.0.0.1:9` signs in successfully THEN the `Location` is `http://127.0.0.1:9/?code=<code>&state=<state>`, with the path `/` added by URL serialisation.

findings.title: Sign-in POST reads username and password from the query before the form body
findings.detail: param() returns the query value when one exists and falls back to the form only otherwise. A POST with `username` or `password` in the query therefore ignores the posted form value.
findings.suggested_fix: WHEN a sign-in POST carries `username` both in the query and in the form body THEN the query value is used and the form value is ignored.

findings.title: verifyRs256 also requires the header kid to equal the JWK kid
findings.detail: Design decision 5 says verifyRs256 is true for alg RS256 plus a matching signature. The implementation also returns false when the header kid differs from the JWK's kid, so a token signed by the right key under another kid fails. This affects how 'the current key's signature checks' can be shown for the unknown_kid flaw.
findings.suggested_fix: WHEN `verifyRs256` gets a token signed by the JWK's private key whose header `kid` differs from the JWK's `kid` THEN it returns false.

findings.title: Oversized bodies are read to the end before the 413
findings.detail: readBody keeps consuming data after the limit is passed, discarding it, and answers only at `end`. A huge upload is fully received before the 413 is sent and the socket destroyed.
findings.suggested_fix: WHEN a request body exceeds 65536 bytes THEN the server reads and discards the whole body before it answers 413 `{"error":"invalid_request"}` and destroys the socket.

findings.title: Leftover scaffold stub comments and a misleading close error code
findings.detail: jwt.ts and keys.ts still begin with 'Signature stub (milestone scaffold...)' although they are now implemented. close() rejects with FAKE_OIDC_START_FAILED when the server fails to close.
evidence: test/support/fake-oidc/server.ts: `reject(new FakeOidcError("FAKE_OIDC_START_FAILED", "server did not close", { cause: error }));`
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the stub comments and use a fitting error for a failed close.

findings.title: Userinfo accepts an ID token as the bearer
findings.detail: liveAccessToken in session.ts checks the signature, iss, exp and sid, but never typ. A valid ID token (typ "ID") sent as a bearer gets a 200 profile, although the requirement says "live access token". No scenario pins this.
evidence: test/support/fake-oidc/session.ts: function liveAccessToken(provider: Provider, token: string): DecodedJwt | undefined { const decoded = verifiedToken(provider, token); ...
findings.suggested_fix: WHEN userinfo is called with a valid, unexpired ID token of a live session as the bearer THEN it answers 200 with the profile claims.

findings.title: mintJwt treats an unknown kind as an ID token
findings.detail: mintJwt picks access claims only when kind === "access". Any other value, for example "refresh" cast in, silently gives an ID token, where unknown user, client and flaw all throw.
findings.suggested_fix: WHEN mintToken gets a kind other than "id" or "access" THEN it returns a valid ID token without throwing.

findings.title: wrong_nonce without a nonce yields "-mismatch"
findings.detail: applyClaimFlaw writes `${nonce ?? ""}-mismatch`, so wrong_nonce with no nonce option gives nonce "-mismatch". No scenario covers it.
findings.suggested_fix: WHEN mintToken gets flaw wrong_nonce and no nonce THEN the token's nonce claim is "-mismatch".
